correspondence.component_scope: Western opening and Queijada connection
correspondence.finding: The western opening lies in the Próximo Itupeva setting of Lajedão. The original draws its small feeder into the east-going Córrego das Vacas corridor and onward into the mapped Queijada course. The latter bends through the Alto da Colina/Kaylua setting to the Rio do Meio corridor. The whole opening and connector are visible at ordinary corridor scale; the short initial feeder itself is not assigned a name.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale; tidal channel correspondence does not imply uniform flow or naming.

correspondence.component_scope: Rio do Meio and Ibirapuã/Pato corridor
correspondence.finding: The mapped watercourse continues southeast past Vila Betinho and receives Córrego Jequitibá before the Ibirapuã area. The connected route then passes the Ibirapuã/Pato setting and continues southeast and east toward the lower Rio do Pato. The city-side Ribeirão do Pato labeling and downstream Rio do Pato labeling are retained as local map observations; neither is imposed on the initial feeder.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale; tidal channel correspondence does not imply uniform flow or naming.

correspondence.component_scope: Peruípe Sul and Norte junctions
correspondence.finding: The selected Pato corridor joins the Peruípe do Sul system, then reaches the mapped confluence with Rio Peruípe Norte upstream from Helvécia. The separate northern arm is mapped through the Córrego do Vinho setting. The selected continuation is the downstream Peruípe corridor through Helvécia; the branch names remain distinct.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale; tidal channel correspondence does not imply uniform flow or naming.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower inland corridor and northward estuarine connection
correspondence.finding: The original follows the watercourse east through the Helvécia and São José do Peruípe area into the lowland bend by Juerana, Santa Luzia and Dendê. The selected northward continuation is geographically represented by the connected Rio Peixoto/estuarine channel corridor along the western edge of the Cassurubá mangroves, which reaches the Caravelas channel network near Ilha Coqueiro. The original also separately depicts the Peruípe route toward Nova Viçosa. This is geographic channel correspondence, not an assertion of uniform downstream flow in the tidal connections.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale; tidal channel correspondence does not imply uniform flow or naming.

correspondence.component_scope: Estuarine branches and actual sea terminal
correspondence.finding: The terminal setting is the Caravelas–Nova Viçosa tidal estuarine complex, including channels around Cassurubá and Coqueiro and the Rio do Macaco junction by Caravelas. The ICMBio original depicts the northern estuary and ocean connection, and its bounded annex prose expressly locates the Caravelas–Atlantic outlet at Canal do Tomba. The terminal is therefore treated as an Atlantic estuary outlet at ordinary geographic scale. The displayed model sea-extension is not treated as an independently sourced natural river course.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale; tidal channel correspondence does not imply uniform flow or naming.

correspondence.component_scope: Lakes and reservoirs
correspondence.finding: The sheets depict small ponds, lagoons and wet lowlands beside the corridor, including separate water bodies near the lower junction region. No lake or reservoir passage is depicted on the selected through-going corridor. This is bounded original-map evidence, not a basin-wide inventory or a claim that every impoundment is absent.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary component/corridor scale; tidal channel correspondence does not imply uniform flow or naming.

correspondence.component_scope: Western opening, southeast headward descent and southern turn into the northeastward upper corridor
correspondence.finding: All selected headward line parts were read for orientation. The earlier basin-elevation pixels show a western upland network and connected valleys west of Saint-Quentin, but do not securely isolate this complete selected opening and southern turn. The2013 route-map extent omits that region.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Little Main approach and Kedgwick junction, followed by the middle Restigouche to the eastern bend
correspondence.finding: The original route map labels Little Main Restigouche on the southern, upstream approach to the Kedgwick junction, separately labels the Kedgwick tributary and shows their junction at the Montgomery Bridge setting. Downstream Restigouche winds north past the mapped Larry’s Gulch, Red Bank and Whites Brook Island settings, receives the Patapédia from the northwest and turns east. The selected downstream portion of9440 corresponds at ordinary corridor scale.
correspondence.mapped_component_name: Little Main Restigouche River / Restigouche River
correspondence.limits: The Little Main label is not projected backward over the unresolved western opening; Restigouche is not assigned as the uniform name of the entire9440 component.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward lower Restigouche, Upsalquitch junction and northward return toward Matapédia
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor follows the mapped eastward Restigouche past the named camp/landing sequence, the broad southern bend at the Upsalquitch junction near Rafting Ground, and the northward return toward Matapédia. The Upsalquitch is a separate incoming river.

correspondence.component_scope: Post-Matapédia eastern reach and actual selected terminal near Tide Head
correspondence.finding: The map continues the Restigouche east from Matapédia into the widening channel near Tide Head, with Campbellton farther downstream. That channel is the selected terminal setting; the model sea tag does not establish the river’s final open-sea mouth.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected northern tributary from the upper off-map opening to the Matapédia junction
correspondence.finding: The selected branch enters the main corridor at the Matapédia setting. Earlier basin pixels show the northern valley approaching that locality, and publisher prose identifies Matapédia among the basin tributaries. However, the full selected upper branch lies beyond the detailed2013 map and was not securely distinguished in the earlier overview. Its whole-component correspondence and name remain unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern opening and initial westward reach
correspondence.finding: The selected model begins in the east, runs generally west with a short northward excursion, then bends south. Its actual source waterbody or terrain, natural channel, lake and ice associations are unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward deflection and upper southwestward course
correspondence.finding: The model turns distinctly south, then resumes a broadly west-southwest course. No allowed original map establishes this transfer, any material tributary junction or a through-lake connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Long middle west-southwest corridor
correspondence.finding: The model continues west and then southwest across the middle corridor. Actual channel continuity, significant branches and lake passages remain without primary-map correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower westward corridor with a shallow northward return
correspondence.finding: The model bends generally west with a shallow northward return before resuming westward progress. No selected lower-course hydronym, lake connector or natural-river course is established from primary original cartography.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward terminal approach and actual receiving water
correspondence.finding: The model turns south toward its retained sea-classified ending. The actual receiving waterbody and the connection from the lower course to that terminal are not established; the stored sea class is model metadata only.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Q. del Jaguay headward course into the upper Ñaupe setting
correspondence.finding: The PEOT original maps the selected northern approach along Q. del Jaguay, distinguishes the eastern Q. de vacas tributary and carries the drainage south toward Ñaupe. The selected opening is only a bounded part of this mapped drainage; it is not asserted to be the river source. MTC independently shows the corresponding dashed northern channel. No exact formal naming-transition point is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Ñaupe and Capilla de Naupe past El Progreso/El Badén, Querpón and La Victoria/Porvenir
correspondence.finding: The district original labels the selected northern river Ñaupe and maps its successive relationship with the highway, eastern tributary mouths and westward meanders by Querpón and La Victoria. The eastern San Cristóbal course approaching Insculas is a separate feeder, not the selected opening. Tributary labels are not transferred to the full object.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected southern continuation from La Victoria/El Progreso I through the Escute setting to Hualtacal
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues south on the western side of the eastern Insculas/San Cristóbal course and turns toward Hualtacal. PEOT and MTC show portions of this northern drainage but do not depict a continuous connector through the intervening El Progreso I–Escute setting. INGEMMET photograph 1 independently identifies the Insculas–Naupe confluence at Hualtacal Santa Rosa. This supports the tributary relationship without establishing all of the selected connecting corridor.
correspondence.material_gap: Continuous primary-map coverage of the selected La Victoria/El Progreso I–Escute/Hualtacal connector remains incomplete; the confluence photograph alone does not close the intervening route.

correspondence.component_scope: Receiving Hualtacal–La Calera Santa Rosa–Oberasal/Pasaje Norte corridor
correspondence.finding: South of the Hualtacal junction, PEOT traces the selected receiving course through La Calera Santa Rosa toward Oberasal and prints Insculas on this receiving reach. MTC traces the same corridor and prints Río San Cristóbal. These are recorded as source-specific reach labels, without asserting a uniform registered equivalence or moving an official name boundary. Nearby Laguna Larga is a settlement label here and does not establish a selected lake passage.
correspondence.mapped_component_name: Insculas; San Cristóbal (source-dependent mapped reach labels)

correspondence.component_scope: Pasaje Norte/Pasaje Sur junction with the eastern Cascajal approach and the westward Ancol–Ficuar reach
correspondence.finding: The originals distinguish the northern selected approach from the eastern Cascajal course through the Cruz del Puente/Laucha Chica setting. After their junction, the selected course follows the westward trunk through Pasaje Sur, Ancol Chico/Grande and Ficuar. MTC labels Río Cascajal; PEOT labels Cascajal and Q. Cascajal on parts of the westward course. The name is not extended up every selected feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Cerro de Arena–Alto de Roque–Las Pozas and the selected northern continuation toward Sombrero Verde
correspondence.finding: Cascajal is supported west past Cerro de Arena and Alto de Roque to Las Pozas. Near the western split, the clearly drawn receiving channel turns south by La Tranca/Los Positos and then west as Quebrada la Tranca toward Minchales. The selected route instead continues farther north toward the Sombrero Verde setting before crossing PE-04A west of Minchales. Some northern dashed drainage is shown, but no continuous original hydrographic line establishes that selected continuation. The southern La Tranca name is not copied onto it.
correspondence.material_gap: The selected northern branch/continuation beyond the Las Pozas vicinity and its westward PE-04A connector are not continuously established; the mapped southern La Tranca route is not substituted.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwest desert continuation beyond PE-04A toward the PE-1N/El Cruce and La Niña entry setting
correspondence.finding: The MTC adjoining originals show the road sequence, desert and northern lagoon/depression margins, but no continuous hydrographic course follows the selected southwest connector. MINAM prose says ordinary Cascajal flow infiltrates/evaporates in the desert and does not establish this chosen continuation. No irrigation canal or reservoir is inferred from the model line.
correspondence.material_gap: Continuous selected desert-to-depression hydrographic correspondence is missing.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected southward transit within the Laguna La Niña depression and turn toward its coastal margin
correspondence.finding: The Sechura original explicitly labels Laguna La Niña over the broad waterbody crossed by the selected lower route. INGEMMET Figure 14 shows a flood-filled coastal depression in March 2017; MINAM Map 3 shows strongly variable historical extents. These sources establish the waterbody setting, but not all modeled internal passages as one river or the Cascajal name across the lagoon. No lake boundary or shoreline is matched vertex by vertex.
correspondence.material_gap: Broad and event-dependent wetland coverage does not establish the selected internal transfer and exit connections.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected southwest coastal termination
correspondence.finding: Both retained MTC originals place the final selected segment at the La Niña coastal-margin setting, but neither depicts a river or lagoon outlet crossing the coast there. The inspected INGEMMET flood image also does not resolve an outlet at the selected termination. Retained model terminal class sea is not independent proof. This does not assert that transient overflow can never occur.
correspondence.material_gap: The selected actual connection to the Pacific remains unestablished at ordinary corridor scale.
